problems: The dressing repeats three similar oval pads with pastel pebble clusters rather than reading as diverse regenerated meadow.

The ecological sensor caps (0.24 m) and seed-pod cones are invisible at cell scale; nothing says 'future' except the pastel colours.
Blooms are smooth egg spheres 0.6-0.75 m wide, which read as pebbles or eggs rather than flowers.
The dressing is three flat teal discs, each carrying a yellow ellipse, a lilac ellipse and a grey ellipse. They read as lily pads or plates with fried eggs, not clover, flowers and stones
Everything is under 0.1 m and the same pale value as the meadow #9cbea0, so at stream scale the tile is a blank green sheet with three blots
The brief asks for 16 sparse parts spread across the tile; they are bunched into 3 identical clusters
elements.fix: Redistribute the 16 dressing parts into irregular, unequal groupings of clover, angular flower tufts, stones and fallen pods. Give the two tiny sensor caps a distinct manufactured profile, remove the repeated oval bases, and keep most dressing below 0.35 m. / Break the three islands into different shapes and sizes (one long drift ~4x1.2 m, one small 1 m patch, one scattered with no base disc). Replace the bloom eggs with clusters of 3-5 small upright cones or cylinders (0.12-0.2 m wide, 0.25-0.35 m tall) in #efbd66 / #c1b5dc / white. Add 2-3 fallen seed-pod pairs in #bca783. Make one sensor cap more legible: a 0.35 m ivory disc on a 0.3 m navy stalk with the cyan pip. Keep every part below 0.35 m. / Remove the three flat discs. Scatter 14–16 separate items across the whole tile with no clustering: 6 upright grass tufts (cones 0.25 w × 0.35 h) in darker green #5f8f6a; 4 flower heads (spheres 0.18 m on 0.25 m stems) in amber #efbd66 and lavender #8c80b4; 3 irregular stones (squashed spheres 0.4–0.6 m) in #8a948f; 2 brown seed pods #8a795c; and 1 small ivory sensor cap on a navy base. Vary rotation and size so no two match.

problems: Parallel cyan lines and centre dashes reproduce conventional lane-marking language on a slate-grey road.
The walking edge reads as a hard linear border; the required planted drainage seam is not evident.
Road panels are #8f9fb2 slate grey, not the bible's pale ceramic #d7e1e8. In the vignette the road is the darkest surface and reads as asphalt.

Two full-length solid cyan lane lines at z ±2.2 plus a dashed cyan centre line (4 dashes at z 0) is a painted modern lane layout recoloured cyan. The bible explicitly asks for 'sparse cyan guidance seams rather than painted asphalt lanes'.
Two 1.6x0.9 m darker 'repair panels' read as manhole or patch rectangles from today's road; the two tiny glowing edge nodes are the only non-modern element.
Two thin dark lines across the road at x ±2 look like expansion joints on a concrete road.

World rule: rules.kerbs / rules.roadMarkings / rules.walkingEdge: the future keeps sidewalks, kerbs and road markings all true, which is today's street structure and encourages lane-line roads. Set roadMarkings false (navigation is via sparse flush guide emitters, not painted lines). Make the walking edge a level shared surface (kerbs false) separated from the vehicle guidance zone only by the planted drainage seam and low edge nodes, so the street is structurally different from the modern age, not just recoloured.

World rule: surfaces.road: base #d7e1e8 is right, but add an explicit rule that road parts must not be darker than #c6cfd8 and must not lay continuous longitudinal lines; the round-4 street used #8f9fb2 slate and full-length cyan lane lines.
elements.fix: Lighten the road to pale ceramic panels and replace the dashed centreline with sparse, flush guidance seams tied to panel joints. Add a narrow planted drainage slit, retain the 8 m unobstructed carriageway and 2 m walking edges, and resolve the kerb as a shallow 0.08 m accessible transition rather than a rail. / Recolour both road slabs to #d7e1e8 with a faint #c6bfd8 panel grid (cross seams every 3 m, 0.06 m wide, #9aa9c4). Delete the 4 centre dashes and both continuous lane lines. Instead place 6-8 short flush cyan guide emitters (0.6x0.06x0.15 m, glow) in a staggered chevron pair every ~3 m along z ±1.5. Replace the two dark repair rectangles with 4-5 small inset drainage slots (0.8x0.03x0.12 m, #36495e) along z ±3.7. Add 4 low ivory edge nodes (0.3 m dome, cyan pip) per side at the kerb. Lower the dark kerb shadow lines to #9aa9c4 so the road edge reads as soft ceramic, not a black kerb.

elements.fix: Reallocate the 32 parts into a tilted, branching shade-tree trunk with an offset broad crown and a smaller flowering tree with one unmistakably long lateral limb. Shrink the main blossom crown to 3-4 spheres. Vary shade-tree crown spheres between 0.9 and 2.4 m, with one big flattened lobe overhanging the walkway. Give the square a 'moss'/planted inset pattern or a stronger accent (e.g. accent2 #739d97 planted joints at scale 2.5) so living greenery shows on the ground.

World rule: centrepiece: drop the '<2.5 m' and 'transparent' requirements. The town's centre must be its boldest landmark, so allow 4.5 m with a solid amber emblem and continuous orbit rings.
World rule: Daylight glow: cyan emitters on pale ground and pale sky read as grey. Require every glow part to sit on a dark navy backing.
elements.fix: Lower and broaden the four emitter petals around a low dais approximately 4.5 m across. Enlarge the faceted seed emblem, shorten the orbit arcs, and keep the complete image below about 2.5 m; use dark emitter recesses for separation while leaving the physical structure matte. / Make the dais a round, two-step ivory platform (4.5 m and 3.6 m diameter, 0.15 m steps) with a thin cyan inset ring. Keep the top under 2.5 m. Add a ring of 4 low ivory sitting ledges on the lower step so it reads as a gathering point like the bonfire it replaces. / Make it the focal object of the town. Widen the dais to 6 m with three steps (navy #36495e bottom, ivory, lavender top). Replace the four stubby legs with four tall curved ivory petals (2.6 m, leaning inward 15°) with navy inner faces. Make the emblem a solid faceted seed 1.6 m tall in amber #efbd66 with a cyan glow core, floating 2.8–4.4 m. problems: Repeated spherical greenery makes the roof terraces read as stacked topiary rather than inhabited living architecture.

elements.fix: Retain the rounded habitat, dark windows and clear front entrance, but introduce readable recessed growing beds and fewer, more irregular plant masses. Reveal the supporting shell or ribs beneath each upper terrace and separate foliage from roof edges to eliminate ambiguous intersections.

problems: Uniform concentric tiers read as a tapered office tower rather than an identifiable modular habitat.

Seven concentric octagonal tiers of identical navy window bands with ivory slabs read as a wedding cake or beehive, too regular for the bible's 'stepped modular habitat tower'.
The greenery is small mint blobs on a few terrace edges; at stream scale the tower is navy and white stripes.
17.2 m tall but 11 m wide, stepping in sharply every couple of floors: it reads as a wedding cake, beehive or lighthouse, not a skyscraper

The planters are tiny teal bobbles
It reaches z 7.4, off the lot
elements.fix: Break the taper into several staggered clusters of chunky dwelling modules, separated by ivory structural ribs and distinct dark windows. Create readable shared planted terraces with irregular greenery and retain a clear ground entrance within the existing footprint. / Break the symmetry: offset each tier 0.4-1.0 m in alternating directions, and make 2-3 tiers rectangular modules instead of octagons. Run one continuous ivory vertical core with a 0.3 m cyan seam up one side. Put larger green terrace gardens (1.2-1.8 m crowns in #5f8f6a/#8db07a, plus a #739d97 planter rim) on at least four terraces, cantilevered over the edges. Vary the window bands: some full-height dark glazing, some ivory with punched windows. / Make it a tower: a 6 × 6 m base core rising to 17 m with only three setbacks (at 6, 11 and 15 m), each stepping in 0.8 m. Use vertical ivory fins (0.3 m) on the corners for the full height, and dark glazing between floor slabs every 3 m. Put a roof garden with 2–3 real tree crowns (1.5 m) at each setback and a slim mast on top. Keep it inside |x|,|z| ≤ 6.
